P1.evidence: P1a is a clear hit and well done — the rep opened by reading back the goals captured previously so the prospect felt seen: 'we talked about a number of different goals, right? Becoming the best man you can be. We want to address some weaknesses in shoulder up the body. We want to create athleticism to help improve ping pong and other sports, confidence, like dating, you know, have an at-home routine.' P1d ran as a prioritisation variant of the open question: 'Out of all those, like, which would you say is, like, the most important out of all that, out of curiosity?' The four-part frame and frame agreement are marked not applicable because this is the second call and the frame belongs to the first. Phase scored partial rather than hit because no agenda of any kind was set for a call that was always going to end in a payment request — within ninety seconds of the opening question the rep was already asserting fit ('I really think it is going to be a super phenomenal fit') and asking for a commitment to the training frequency.

P2.evidence: Baseline belongs to the first call, which is not in this batch, and the rep makes callbacks confirming it ran — 'you know how we talked about like, you know, eating out, we're not super consistent with it' and 'do you remember how you told me that like, hey, we need to find a program that we can do that's easy, low barrier to entry'. Dropped from the denominator accordingly. Flagged for the reviewer rather than scored: nothing about health conditions, injuries, chronic pain, medications, height, weight or age appears anywhere in this transcript, so this file cannot verify that P2c or P2d were ever asked. The only physical limitation mentioned is posture, and it was raised by the prospect.

P3.evidence: The surface goals were established on the prior call, so P3a to P3c drop out. The rep did reopen the deep work and P3d landed well — asking which goal mattered most produced a genuine why: 'there is a bit of external motivation, like, going to do something that people say that you can't do... when someone says that you can't do something, it almost gives you a lot of fuel to prove them wrong.' That was the moment to drive, and the rep did not. P3e was never asked; instead the rep asserted the answer himself with his own story — 'all of a sudden my dating life is better, my energy is better' — which hands the prospect a benefit rather than making him articulate one. P3f was never asked, though the prospect volunteered a ripple-effect idea unprompted. P3g reached identity strongly ('best version of Michael', 'main character' versus 'NPC') but nothing on family, relationships, legacy or mortality, and the prospect's family circumstances are unknown even now. P3h, the reflect-back, never came. The net effect is that this call carried no emotional weight into the price.

P4.evidence: Run on the prior call. The rep's callbacks show findings already in hand — the low-barrier requirement, the inconsistent eating, the shoulder and upper-body weakness — and he built the training pillar directly on them. Not re-run here and not expected to be. The prospect did volunteer his own root cause during this call, unprompted, when he said he had avoided coaching for years because 'I thought there was a cool factor in just, like, being self-taught', which would have been a strong hook to reflect back and was not used.

P5.evidence: The consequence frame is entirely absent. No version of the two-year question was asked, nothing was said about what happens if nothing changes, the prospect was never asked whether he would settle for that, and no line-in-the-sand moment was created with him. The only appearance of the phrase is the rep using it about other people to justify paying in full — 'the students that really go all in from the get-go, and they're like, no, I'm drawing the line in the sand, I'm going all in, they always get the best results.' There is also no evidence in the rep's callbacks that P5 ran on the previous call, so this is scored as a straight miss rather than dropped. This is the central process failure: the call closed on rapport and enthusiasm with no cost of inaction established anywhere, and it is exactly the kind of close that scores well on outcome and badly on process.

P6.evidence: Both commitment questions ran before the price was quoted, which is the right order. P6a: 'training, nutrition, accountability, all built around your life. you agree that if we have those three things dialed in, like, that's all that we need to get to the best version of Michael possible' — answered 'Yeah, exactly.' P6b: 'if we can figure out all the details, like, are you really fully committed to showing up and doing the work to become the best version of Michael that you can be?' — answered 'Yeah. I'm all in.' The rep also ran a strong unscripted move worth propagating, securing a commitment to communicate when things go wrong: 'if we do this, are you like, are you actually willing to, you know, something comes up to raise, actually raise your hand and get the support and the help that you need?' P6c is partial because hesitation did surface immediately after the price — a payment-plan request plus a disclosed spending constraint — and the script's instruction is to return to Phase 5. There was no Phase 5 to return to, so the rep closed on conviction instead.

P11.evidence: All four steps completed before hanging up, and this is the best-executed phase in the batch so far. Payment collected live and confirmed: 'it went through perfect, man.' Onboarding with Trevor booked, and when the prospect found a conflict the rep rescheduled it on the call rather than leaving it — 'let's just reschedule for Tuesday instead... you should be booked in for the 515 on Tuesday Eastern.' Agreement confirmed arrived and signed on the call: 'can you pop that open and just do a quick autograph on it for me?' followed by an explicit submission check. Step four covered: 'go check all the automated emails, read through everything, sign up for school', plus the onboarding form texted across live with a time estimate. Process note that does not change the score: the agreement terms including the guarantee were only explained after payment, when the prospect asked what the performance reward credit was, and he signed saying 'I'll just skim in real quick.'

objection_plays.detail: The trigger is unambiguous and was raised twice: 'is it possible to have like a payment plan?' and then 'I could probably put down the fixed grand right now, unless there's an option to space it out a bit', alongside a disclosed constraint — 'I've like spent so much in the last like two, three months that it's like, I honestly probably need to start holding back a little bit.' Essentially none of the play ran. No isolation question. No 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place'. Critically, the scripted line that directly answers what he asked — 'Most clients pay upfront, but for some we break it up. Want to explore making it work?' — was never said, so the prospect never learned whether a plan exists. No permission question about discussing finances openly, and none of the six financial-picture questions: cash on hand, monthly surplus, number of credit cards, available credit per card, used versus available, or investments. What the rep substituted was a personal spending anecdote and a conviction close: 'Dude, I think if you can do it all right now, I think you should.' It worked commercially — the card was charged minutes later — which is precisely why this needs coaching rather than praise. Note that the prospect was checking a card limit while paying, which is the exact circumstance the financial-picture questions exist to surface.

notes: A close that flatters the rep and should not. P11 was textbook and the pillar delivery was clean, but the front half of the process simply did not happen on this call: no consequence frame at all, no reflect-back, and no emotional stake established before a $6,000 ask. When money friction surfaced the rep answered a direct question with an anecdote and pushed for payment in full. Two coaching actions. First, run P5 on second calls too — a returning prospect is not a pre-framed one. Second, when a prospect asks whether a payment plan exists, tell him, then run the financial picture; deflecting a direct commercial question is the single riskiest thing on this recording.
